brief.title: Why Money Was Even Invented
brief.hook: Money exists to solve one deeply annoying problem.

sections.label: Hook
sections.narration: What if money was invented just to fix one deeply annoying problem?

sections.label: The problem
sections.narration: Before money there was barter. And barter only works if the other person happens to want exactly what you have. Economists call it the double coincidence of wants.
sections.visual: text — "The double coincidence of wants" | "Both traders must want what the other has."

sections.label: Why it fails
sections.narration: You have eggs and you want shoes. But the shoemaker doesn't want eggs. Now you're chasing a three-way trade. As towns grew and people specialized, that got nearly impossible.
sections.visual: text — "Barter doesn't scale" | "Specialization made matches too rare."

sections.label: The fix
sections.narration: So people started accepting one thing almost everyone wanted: salt, grain, metal. A universally wanted good let you split a trade in two. Sell now, buy later.
sections.visual: text — "A universally-wanted good" | "Sell now, buy later."

sections.label: First coins
sections.narration: Around 630 BCE, the kingdom of Lydia stamped the first standardized coins out of electrum, and the idea spread across the ancient world.

sections.label: Payoff
sections.narration: So money isn't really about gold or paper. It's a shared agreement that turns one impossible trade into two easy ones.
sections.visual: text — "Money is an agreement" | "One impossible trade becomes two easy ones."

facts.text: Barter requires a 'double coincidence of wants' — both traders must want what the other has.
Money emerged as a universally-wanted medium so each half of a transaction could be separated (Adam Smith).
facts.sourceTitle: The Double Coincidence of Wants — Globalgood

facts.text: The Mesopotamian shekel (~5,000 years ago) was the first known currency; debt records predate coins.
facts.sourceTitle: When and why did people first start using money? — The Conversation

facts.text: The first standardized coins were struck in Lydia (modern Turkey) around 630 BCE from electrum.
